sources.entry: Zulip - Zulip is a powerful, open source group chat application. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Python

summary.one_liner: Zulip is an open-source team chat app that uses topic-based threading to combine aspects of email and chat for live and asynchronous conversation.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Zulip as an open-source team chat application built around topic-based threading, which organizes conversations by topic within streams. It positions itself for both live and asynchronous communication. The README says it is developed by a distributed community and names Fortune 500 companies and open source projects among its users. It explains how to get started as a contributor (code, documentation, translation, issue reporting) and as a user. For running it, the README points to self-hosting on Ubuntu or Debian Linux, in Docker, or with prebuilt images for Digital Ocean and Render. It also points to Zulip Cloud as a hosted option. Details on installation steps are not in this README and are linked to external documentation.
use_cases: running a Slack alternative on own server
how_to_run: Self-host directly on Ubuntu or Debian Linux (see linked self-hosting docs)
Deploy prebuilt images for Digital Ocean or Render (see linked docs)
Or use Zulip Cloud hosting instead of running a server
notable: Topic-based threading that combines email-style organization with chat
Designed for both live and asynchronous conversations
Multiple self-hosting paths: Ubuntu/Debian, Docker, prebuilt Digital Ocean and Render images
Large, active contributor community with extensive documentation
caveats: The README does not give detailed installation steps; it links to external self-hosting documentation
Zulip Cloud hosting is offered as an alternative to self-hosting, with paid tiers implied by the mention of a Standard plan
